ruling.recommended_action: Decline the refund request; keep the $6.61 cancellation fee as charged and inform the rider of the voucher/appeal route under NS-7.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a driver-cancellation with a rider-no-show allegation, so it enters only through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver ([F4]) and the driver's basis for cancelling was non-appearance ([F11], [F13]), which routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 [NS-0]. The $6.61 charged is the published cancellation fee on the record ([F7]) and no surge applied ([F8]), so the only question is whether the NS-1 conditions were met.

All three NS-1 elements are settled by the trace and the records. Arrival confirmation (i): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 ([F6]); the trace marks this confirmed by driver_tap, not by platform auto-detection, and the earlier platform arrival at 14:03:20 ([F5]) does not substitute for the tap requirement [NS-1]. Position at the tap (ii): the GPS placed the car 178 m from the pickup at the tap moment ([F6]), inside the 200 m arrival radius applied by the data layer (the radius is a data-layer parameter, not a policy threshold), and the car had been within 200 m since 14:03:20 with a closest approach of 40 m ([F2], [F1]) — so the rider's C1/C2 argument that 178 m "fails" (ii) is an argument against the radius itself, not against the record [NS-1]. Continuous wait after the tap (iii): F6 records 220 s (3 min 40 s) continuously inside the radius after the tap, above the NS-1 default of more than 3 minutes; the GPS trace covering the wait has no hole, and the car was stationary from 14:05:55 to the 14:09:55 cancellation ([F3]) [NS-1]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped ([F12]), so the sequence can be read directly: the driver gave his position and vehicle at 14:06 ([F9]), the rider said at 14:07 she was at the entrance and could not see him ([F10]), and the driver cancelled at 14:09 after noting he had waited more than 3 minutes ([F11]) [NS-1]. The rider's F10 message is her own statement of where she was, not a GPS record, and it is consistent with the measured facts: the car was not at the entrance, but it was within the arrival radius the policy contemplates [NS-1].

Because (i), (ii) and (iii) all hold, NS-2 is not triggered: there is no element failure to justify a refund of the $6.61 [NS-2]. The driver's written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes ([F13]) is a self-serving post-trip claim (G11) and I do not use it — it is unnecessary, because the GPS and timeline records independently satisfy the elements [NS-1]. Traffic facts ([F14], [F15]) and weather ([F16]) are irrelevant to a no-show fee. On NS-7 the rider's dispute is timely ([F4], [F5]), but NS-7 governs only the form and window of a refund once one is due; since no fee waiver or refund condition is met, no voucher issues [NS-7]. The ride-hailing fairness point that the driver parked 179 m from the pin ([F3]) while the rider stood at the entrance ([F10]) is a service-quality matter the rider can raise with RydeHELP, but on this record the fee was chargeable and the complaint fails.

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages ([F9], [F10], [F11]), the rider's complaint text and the driver's statement ([F13]). Message F11 ("Waited more than 3 min, cancelling") is a factual cancellation notice, F10 is a rider searching for the car, and F9 gives vehicle and location; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in the record. Finding: none [SAFE-1].

Evidence: the record settles every element this ruling needs — the arrival tap and its GPS distance, the continuous in-radius wait with no trace hole, the cancellation time, and the amount charged — so the evidence is sufficient and no gap is named [NS-1], [NS-2]. The rider advocate withdrew the flag_account limbs (C5, C6) and RD-6 is not engaged in any event because the driver is not held in breach here [RD-6].

Standing 179 m from the pin while remaining inside the arrival radius is what NS-1 (ii)/(iii) measure; the policy requires position within the arrival area, not the rider's entrance (F3, F6) [NS-1]. The rider's F10 message is her statement, not a GPS record.

The driver did communicate his position and vehicle at 14:06 before the rider's 14:07 message (F9, F10), and the record shows he then stayed inside the radius a further 3 min 40 s before cancelling at 14:09 (F6, F11); 'no reply' does not negate the measured wait (F3, F6) [NS-1].
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are satisfied (F6, F5, F12), NS-2 is not triggered and no full refund arises; the $6.61 is the published cancellation fee (F7, F8) [NS-2].
Withdrawn by the rider in rebuttal; and the tap at 178 m (F6) is inside the arrival radius, so there is no abuse-of-button basis under NS-2 (F6) [NS-2].
Withdrawn by the rider in rebuttal; and RD-6 requires the present dispute to be established against the driver, which it is not (F18, F6) [RD-6].
Timeliness is accepted (F4, F5), but NS-7 only governs the form of a refund once one is due; no refund is due here (F7) [NS-7].

The conclusion (NS-1 (ii) satisfied) is correct, but D3 rests on the 200 m data-layer radius alone while the trace settles (ii) on F6's measured 178 m; the radius is an implementation parameter and I do not cite it as a policy threshold (F6) [NS-1].

The rider's 14:07 message (F10) does not by itself show she was not at the pickup point — she states she was at the entrance; the no-show finding rests on the measured in-radius wait and the completed three-element test, not on that message (F10, F6, F3) [NS-1].

F4 and F10 alone would not establish the no-show; the finding rests on the NS-1 elements measured in F6 and the complete chat record in F12, and F18 (profile) cannot decide the case (F18, F12) [NS-1].
